newsitem.title: USA: Virus Research phase I trial succeeds.
newsitem.headline: Virus Research phase I trial succeeds.

text.p: Virus Research Institute Inc said Tuesday it successfully completed a Phase I study of an influenza vaccine formulated with Adjumer, its proprietary delivery system for injected vaccines.
The results showed that the vaccine was well tolerated and elicited improved immune responses in the vaccinated patients.
Based on the findings it said that Pasteur Merieux Connaught plans to initiate a Phase II study of the Adjumer-formulated vaccine later this year, it said.
Pasteur Merieux Connaught, part of the Rhone-Poulenc group is the new trade name of Pasteur Merieux Serum et Vaccins SA.
Lyon, France,-based Pasteur Merieux operates subsidiaries worldwide, including Connaught Laboratories, which operates in North America.

Jean-Jacques Bertrand, chairman and chief executive officer of Pasteur Merieux Connaught said, "We look forward to pursuing the development of this much improved influenza vaccine product which we expect, upon successful completion of clinical development, to expand the market and bring improved health benefits to a broader segment of the population."
The Phase I trial conducted in France by Pasteur Merieux Connaught was designed to measure the safety and level of immune response of an influenza vaccine formulated with Adjumer.
Some 48 young and 41 elderly adults were given single injections of either an influenza vaccine formulated with Adjumer, or the same vaccine without Adjumer, it said.

A range of Adjumer concentrations were tested, with improved immune responses observed for each dosage level, it said. Side effects were minimal, transient and comparable to those observed in the control group, it added.
